metadata.file_name: Socially Jetlagged and Late for School  Chronotypes  Achievement and Truancy among 15-Year-Old Students in PISA 2018.pdf
metadata.title: Socially Jetlagged and Late for School: Chronotypes, Achievement and Truancy among 15-Year-Old Stude

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the German PISA 2018 subsample (n=5451 students in 223 schools) and conducts all analyses with the R package BIFIEsurvey, which is designed for PISA’s complex survey design and incorporates the appropriate sampling weights and plausible-value procedures. The dependent variable (truancy index) is analyzed together with PISA reading proficiency and other German-administered measures, while the authors explicitly state that analyses account for the stratified sampling structure and all ten plausible values from the PISA reading domain. The paper does not report a specific weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT), but the use of BIFIEsurvey implies weight-aware estimation. No additional preprocessing exclusions (e.g., outlier trimming or missing-data rules) are described in the provided text, beyond the use of the available German PISA subsample and the two school-type splits (Gymnasium vs non-Gymnasium).

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The manuscript reports that analyses were carried out using BIFIEsurvey and that all ten plausible values from the PISA reading domain were used, but it does not describe how missing questionnaire or derived-variable values were handled (e.g., complete-case vs imputation). This is a reporting gap because missingness handling can affect the effective analytic sample and regression coefficients, especially for a composite truancy index and derived social jet lag variables. The paper therefore provides insufficient transparency to fully assess robustness to missing data.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the German PISA 2018 subsample with the nationally added circadian/chronotype questionnaire items to construct social jet lag (CHRONOSJL). The dependent variable is a truancy index formed by summing three PISA student questionnaire items (skip whole day, skip single lessons, arrive late) over the past two full school weeks. Analyses were split into two school-type groups: Gymnasium (GYMI=2) and non-Gymnasium secondary school types combined (GYMI=1), with sample sizes reported as n=2042 for Gymnasium and n=3409 for non-Gymnasium. The paper states that analyses account for PISA’s stratified sampling structure and use all ten plausible values for the PISA reading domain; no further inclusion/exclusion criteria are specified in the provided text.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Germany (15-year-olds) — Reading literacy (PVs) + German grade + BEFKI figural intelligence; outcome: truancy index
main_findings.performance_metrics: Stepwise linear regression (separate by school type). Non-Gymnasium: Model A R²=0.0056 (p=0.1202); Model B R²=0.0214 (p=0.0381); Model C R²=0.0923 (p=0.0000). Gymnasium: Model A R²=0.0011 (p=0.6053); Model B R²=0.0102 (p=0.1371); Model C R²=0.0495 (p=0.0006). Key coefficients in Model C: Non-Gymnasium — CHRONOSJL b=0.0985 (SE=0.0288, t=3.4200, p=0.0015); PVREAD b=-0.2593 (SE=0.0341, t=-7.6000, p=0.0000). Gymnasium — CHRONOSJL b=0.0769 (SE=0.0367, t=2.1000, p=0.0440); PVREAD b=-0.1808 (SE=0.0432, t=-4.1900, p=0.0002).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Germany the study leveraged Social jet lag (CHRONOSJL), PISA reading proficiency (PVREAD), German grade (ordered), socioeconomic status (ESCS), and figural intelligence (BEFKI WLE) to predict Students' truancy (TRUANCY index), finding that social jet lag is a significant positive predictor of truancy in both Gymnasium and non-Gymnasium schools while higher PISA reading proficiency is a significant negative predictor (stronger in non-Gymnasium). This indicates that incorporating chronotype-derived social jet lag measures into large-scale assessment reporting could help identify students at higher risk of missing school, supporting targeted scheduling or support interventions, though the regression design is correlational and cannot establish causality.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes the German PISA 2018 subsample (n=5451 students in 223 schools) and uses a nationally added chronotype module to construct social jet lag (CHRONOSJL) from an adapted Munich Chronotype Questionnaire. Truancy is measured via a formative index combining three self-reported items (skipping whole days, skipping lessons, arriving late) and is modeled with stepwise linear regression separately for Gymnasium versus non-Gymnasium school types. The authors account for PISA’s stratified sampling structure and use all ten plausible values for the PISA reading domain via BIFIEsurvey. In the final models, social jet lag significantly predicts higher truancy in both school groups (non-Gymnasium: b=0.0985, p=0.0015; Gymnasium: b=0.0769, p=0.0440), while PISA reading proficiency significantly predicts lower truancy (non-Gymnasium: b=-0.2593, p<0.001; Gymnasium: b=-0.1808, p<0.001). Explained variance remains modest (R² up to 0.0923), and the paper emphasizes that PISA’s design does not allow causal inference; additionally, missing-data handling for non-PV variables is not reported in the provided text.
